record.context_brief: Control under mean-field and graph limits
record.original_question: When a multi-agent system is represented across several limiting descriptions, including microscopic dynamics, mean-field limits, graph limits, and embedding-based representations, how do optimal control problems behave under those limiting procedures? In particular, when passing between these scales, what properties of the control problem are preserved, changed, or lost?

evidence.quote: In [95] the authors show other connections via mean-field, graph-limit, and embeddings. A future direction of great interest will be to understand how control problems behave with respect to such limits, as in the spirit of Section 4.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-agent system whose state can be described at several scales and through several limiting procedures:

1. A microscopic description by a system of N coupled ordinary differential equations
   x_i'(t) = F(x_i(t), (x_j(t))_{j=1..N}, u_i(t)),  i = 1,...,N,
   where x_i(t) ∈ R^d is the state of agent i and u_i ∈ U_ad is a control taking values in a fixed admissible control set;

2. A mean-field description, in which as N → ∞ the empirical measure μ^N_t = (1/N) Σ δ_{x_i(t)} converges to a probability measure μ_t solving a continuity/Vlasov-type PDE
   ∂_t μ_t + div(V[μ_t, ν_t] μ_t) = 0,
   driven by a measure-valued control ν_t;

3. A graph-limit (graphon) description, in which the interaction weights w_{ij}^N converge to a graphon W: [0,1]^2 → R and the agent population converges to a continuum of agents indexed by α ∈ [0,1] whose state x(t,α) evolves according to an integro-differential equation involving W;

4. An embedding-based description, in which agents are represented as points/measures in a common Hilbert or Wasserstein space, and the dynamics and controls are formulated in this embedding.

Associated to each level is an optimal control problem of minimizing a cost functional J of the form
   J = ∫_0^T L(state, control) dt + Φ(state(T))
   subject to the corresponding dynamics, over admissible controls in U_ad.

Problem. Develop a rigorous theory of optimal control under these limiting procedures. Specifically:

(a) Identify conditions on F, L, Φ, the interaction kernels, and the admissible controls under which the value functions and optimal controls of the microscopic problems converge (e.g., in the sense of Γ-convergence) to those of the mean-field, graphon, and embedding-based control problems, and characterize the limit problems explicitly.

(b) Determine which structural properties of the control problem (existence of optimizers, Pontryagin-type optimality conditions, dynamic programming / Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equations, controllability, stability of optimal trajectories, regularity of the value function) are preserved when passing between any two of these descriptions, and which are altered or lost.

(c) Establish the commutativity (or quantify the failure of commutativity) of the diagram whose vertices are the four control problems and whose edges are the mean-field limit, the graph limit, and the embedding maps.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Γ-convergence of finite-agent optimal controls to mean-field optimal controls is established in several settings, and graphon mean-field control frameworks (including on sparse graphs) have been developed recently. However, a unified theory describing how optimal control problems behave simultaneously under mean-field, graph-limit, and embedding limits, and which control-theoretic properties are preserved across all these procedures, has not been established and is widely cited as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Mean-field optimal control as Gamma-limit of finite agent controls
status_evidence.snippet: Γ-convergence shows that optimal strategies for finite dimensional problems converge to optimal strategies of the infinite dimensional mean-field problem.
status_evidence.claim: Mean-field limit of optimal control problems is partially understood via Γ-convergence.

status_evidence.title: Graphon Mean-Field Control for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
status_evidence.snippet: A discrete-time graphon mean-field control framework approximates cooperative heterogeneous MARL on large graphs by combining classical MFC and network games.
status_evidence.claim: Graph-limit (graphon) control frameworks exist but are developed separately from mean-field limits.

status_evidence.title: Mean-Field Control on Sparse Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A framework for MFC on large sparse graphs redefining the system state as a probability measure over decorated rooted neighborhoods.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends control to sparse graph limits, but a unified theory across all limiting descriptions remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Optimal control of mean-field limit of multiagent systems with and without common noise
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to develop optimal control under mean-field limits.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research indicates the unified problem is still active.
